one-line thesis: Aequs delivered a landmark FY26 with 33% revenue growth and a $889M aerospace order book, but consolidated PAT remains negative due to aggressive consumer electronics capex depreciation. The investment thesis hinges on achieving consumer EBITDA breakeven by Q4FY27 and sustaining 20%+ aerospace margins as new Hosur and Karnataka capacities commission.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 12,304 Cr (+33% YoY); EBITDA: INR 1,545 Cr (+43% YoY, 13% margin); PAT: Loss of INR 1,133 Cr (improved from -11% to -9% margin); Order Book: $889 Mn (Aerospace only); Net Debt/Equity: 0.23x. One-offs/Distortions: Q4 PAT loss of INR 541 Cr driven by full run-rate depreciation on new consumer capex before utilization ramped; Aerospace segment EBITDA margin of 27% includes other income, operational margin guided at 20%.
guidance: FY27 Revenue Growth: 45-50% consolidated (Aerospace 25-30%, Consumer 125-150%); Margins: Aerospace ~20% EBITDA, Consumer to reach EBITDA breakeven by Q4FY27; Order Inflow: Continued addition of 100+ SKUs/quarter in Aerospace; Capex: INR 660 Cr total (INR 160 Cr Aerospace, INR 500 Cr Consumer).
order book & pipeline: $889 million in Aerospace (approx. 8-9x trailing aerospace revenue); robust visibility driven by 433 new parts added in Q4 alone (total portfolio 5,654 SKUs); long-term agreements with global OEMs for engine and landing gear components.
segment / subsidiary detail: Aerospace: Revenue INR 10,464 Cr (+27% YoY), EBITDA INR 2,813 Cr (+76% YoY), ROCE 20%. Consumer: Revenue INR 1,840 Cr (+84% YoY), EBITDA Loss INR 783 Cr (loss widened due to new capacity commissioning); utilization currently 23%, targeting 40-50% in FY27.
growth verticals / optionality: New INR 1,900 Cr MoU for vertically integrated aero-engine/landing gear park in Hosur (Tamil Nadu); INR 2,856 Cr expansion in Belagavi/Hubballi; moving up value chain into engine components (revenue impact from FY28); PLI scheme eligibility starting FY27.
margins & cost dynamics: Aerospace margins sustained at ~20% operational level despite mix changes; Consumer margins depressed by low utilization (23%) and high fixed depreciation; material cost inflation (titanium/steel) passed through to customers via long-term agreements; logistics costs up slightly due to West Asia crisis but deemed non-material.
capex / expansion: FY27 planned capex INR 660 Cr (INR 160 Cr Aerospace, INR 500 Cr Consumer); FY26 saw significant asset base expansion leading to gross block of ~INR 830 Cr in Consumer; funding via borrowings and internal accruals; depreciation run-rate ~INR 45-46 Cr/quarter plus additions.
capital allocation: Prioritizing capacity expansion for confirmed customer demand (Mattel, Apple ecosystem); net debt/equity improved to 0.23x post-IPO; cash balance INR 3,015 Cr; no dividend mentioned, reinvestment mode for growth.
risks & watch-items: Consumer segment ramp-up delay beyond Q4FY27; dependency on single large consumer electronics customer; geopolitical supply chain disruptions (West Asia) impacting logistics and raw material lead times (Titanium 52 weeks, Steel 65-75 weeks); key management change (CFO stepping down); equipment sourcing constraints from China.
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term structural growth and moat (vertical integration, speed-to-market); transparent about short-term P&L pain from consumer capex; pragmatic on working capital buildup due to geopolitical stocking; committed to margin recovery via utilization.
non-obvious takeaways: Aerospace segment EBITDA margin of 27% reported includes other income and excludes unallocated corporate costs; true operational margin is ~20%; Consumer electronics and Aerospace share 'precision manufacturing' platform capabilities but use distinct machine bases (CNC for metal/aero/electronics vs. Molding for plastics/toys); PLI benefits only start accruing in FY27.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain de-risking and China+1 strategy driving orders to India | Aequs Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of global OEMs shifting sourcing to India; unique position with vertically integrated capabilities and large order book. |
| Raw material inflation and logistics disruption | Indian Aerospace Suppliers without long-term contracts | loser | Med | Players without pass-through mechanisms or long-term material coverage will suffer margin compression from titanium/steel price spikes and logistics delays. |

themes.title: Commercial-aerospace supply chain (Boeing/Airbus/engine OEMs)
themes.need: A record global commercial-aircraft backlog plus engine-OEM (GE/Safran/Honeywell/RR/P&W) outsourcing and China+1 are pulling Indian build-to-print suppliers up the value chain - aero-engine hot-section airfoils, airframe structures, tooling and wire harnesses. AZAD ramping engine/airfoil exports; UNIMECH near-tripling tooling capacity; AEQUS/SANSERA on precision aero; ROSSTECH on harnesses; PTCIL on titanium castings.

themes.title: Electronics manufacturing (EMS) & Make-in-India localization
themes.need: PLI + import-substitution + global China+1 sourcing drive an electronics-manufacturing build-out across consumer durables, defence and components. AMBER/PGEL/EPACK/SYRMA/AVALON/CYIENTDLM on box-build/EMS; DIXON-tier scale; CPPLUS/CNL on surveillance; KAYNES/SYRMA on integrated components; appliance ODMs (EPACK, AMBER) ride RAC/white-goods localization.
themes.driver: PLI disbursement + new ODM/OEM program wins; appliance season; defence/aero EMS conversion (AVALON, CYIENTDLM).

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Aequs Limited manufactures precision-engineered components, forgings and aerostructure assemblies for the aerospace industry and high-value consumer products including toys, kitchen and home appliances and precision device enclosures for consumer electronics. It sells only to institutional B2B customers - global aircraft OEMs and Tier-1 system integrators, and global consumer brands - under long-term, programme-based agreements. Its differentiator is an integrated 'ecosystem' model that clusters specialised manufacturing capabilities, infrastructure and partnerships on connected platforms, proven at Belagavi over fifteen years and now being extended to Hubballi and Hosur.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Rising aircraft production rates are increasing demand across the programs in which Aequs participates
- Global OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers are seeking to simplify fragmented supply chains and work with partners capable of absorbing larger and more complex work packages - favouring Aequs' qualified portfolio, delivery record and vertically integrated ecosystem
- Aerospace programme life-cycles often extend over several decades with rigorous qualification and stringent quality standards, creating significant barriers to entry and durable revenue visibility
- Consumer Electronics fixed cost base is substantially in place while volumes are still ramping; as volumes scale, stronger fixed-cost absorption and operating leverage are expected to carry the segment towards sustainable profitability
- Reported net loss is driven by depreciation and finance costs on capacity commissioned over the last twenty-four months plus the ramping Consumer Electronics cost base - described as an investment cycle 'now behind us in spending terms and ahead of us in returns'
- Balance sheet strengthened materially during the year; together with retained IPO proceeds this gives headroom to invest without straining the capital structure
- Global aerospace industry growth driven by rising air travel, higher aircraft production, MRO expansion for ageing fleets and increased outsourcing to Tier-1/Tier-2 suppliers as OEMs focus on design and final assembly
- India offers a significant cost advantage through competitive labour costs and lower overheads versus US and European aerospace hubs; Make in India, Aatmanirbhar Bharat, PLI and favourable SEZ policies support the sector
- Indian aerospace manufacturing market projected to reach Rs 257.09 Bn ($3.06 Bn) by 2030, with the largest projected 2030 sub-segments being aerostructures, landing systems and actuation systems
- Threats flagged for the industry: dependence on imported raw materials and components exposing manufacturers to supply-chain disruption, geopolitical risk and input-cost volatility; and a mismatch between education and industry requirements limiting job-ready talent
- Consumer durables demand supported by rising domestic demand, rapid urbanization, an expanding middle class and improving product affordability; India's consumer durables/electricals/EMS sector expected to see gradual recovery
- Global EMS market projected to grow from $689.86 Bn in CY2026 to $1,192.68 Bn by CY2034 (7.10% CAGR); global toys market to reach $223.74 Bn by CY2035 (6.62% CAGR); global cookware to grow from $38.34 Bn in 2026 to $67.87 Bn by CY2034 (7.40% CAGR)
- Educational and skill-building toys gaining prominence as parents increasingly view learning-and-play products as developmental rather than discretionary
- Indian cookware demand shifting toward premium, health-conscious and induction-compatible categories (hard-anodized, tri-ply stainless steel) as incomes rise; Indian cookware market expected to reach $5.70 Bn by 2034
- Aerospace order book stood at USD 889 million as at March 31, 2026, described as robust and supporting improved revenue visibility
- Aerospace portfolio expanded to 5,654 SKUs during the year; each new part undergoes rigorous qualification and is typically tied to a long-term programme, which deepens customer relationships and improves revenue visibility
- Company enters FY 2026-27 with a substantial Aerospace order book and growing Consumer programs
- Aerospace parts supplied for single-aisle platforms (A220, A320, B737) and long-range platforms (A330, A350, B767, B777, B787)

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing capacity expansion for confirmed customer demand (Mattel, Apple ecosystem); net debt/equity improved to 0.23x post-IPO; cash balance INR 3,015 Cr; no dividend mentioned, reinvestment mode for growth.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Aequs signed MoUs with the Governments of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, including a Rs 1,900 crore investment at Hosur to establish an integrated aerospace ecosystem focused on aero-engine components and complex landing-gear components; the Chairman describes the Tamil Nadu MoU as an intent to invest that amount over ten years. Separately, and as a firm commitment, the Company has approved cumulative investment of Rs 2,856 crore over five years across its Belagavi and Hubballi clusters in Karnataka to expand aerospace precision engineering and consumer manufacturing capacity. Commercial production for Consumer Electronics commenced during Q3 FY26, with further investments planned for FY27 including the ongoing construction of a new facility at Hubballi to support higher production volumes and meet growing customer demand. At Hosur the immediate focus is a phased execution plan, with investment sequenced against customer requirements, identified programme opportunities and the specialised capabilities that aero-engine and landing-gear components demand - management frames it as 'no ordinary greenfield, but one built on the considerable aerospace execution knowledge already established at Belagavi'. Across Belagavi and Hubballi, investment is directed towards strengthening manufacturing capability, supporting programme scale-up and improving operational readiness; as recently commissioned capacities mature the emphasis shifts to utilization, productivity improvement and operating leverage. The Company intends to phase investment in line with customer requirements, programme visibility and capability needs, funded off a balance sheet that strengthened materially during the year together with retained IPO proceeds. Reported capacity utilization stands at 62% for Aerospace (against a stated India average of 70%) and 23% for Consumer, leaving substantial headroom in recently commissioned assets. Other capability-building steps during the year include a partnership with IIT Dharwad to establish an advanced materials R&D ecosystem, and Ajna Aerospace and Defense (established 2026) which aims to build an end-to-end Unmanned Aerial Systems ecosystem spanning integration, manufacturing, testing and commercialization.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on long-term structural growth and moat (vertical integration, speed-to-market); transparent about short-term P&L pain from consumer capex; pragmatic on working capital buildup due to geopolitical stocking; committed to margin recovery via utilization.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated ecosystem model clustering specialised manufacturing, infrastructure and partnerships lets customers reduce complexity and source a broader range of requirements from one platform - proven at Belagavi over fifteen years
- Qualified and single-sourced on most of its parts, with each new part undergoing rigorous qualification and typically tied to a long-term programme, creating high barriers to entry
- Portfolio expanded to 5,654 SKUs during the year, deepening customer relationships and revenue visibility
- Aerospace order book of USD 889 million as at March 31, 2026 provides multi-year revenue visibility
- Blue-chip global customer base of aircraft OEMs, Tier-1 integrators and global toy brands under long-term, programme-based agreements
- Vertically integrated ecosystem positions the company to absorb larger and more complex work packages as OEMs consolidate fragmented supply chains
- Nearly two decades of aerospace execution knowledge established at Belagavi, which de-risks the Hosur greenfield
- Advanced materials R&D collaboration with IIT Dharwad covering material characterization, failure analysis and process simulation

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Move up the manufacturing value chain by expanding 5-axis machining and manufacturing more critical engine and landing systems, including new parts such as torque tube, engine nacelles and blades.**
- **Diversify customer base in the Aerospace Segment by developing new relationships and entering long-term master service agreements (MSAs).**
- **Grow portfolio of consumer electronics and consumer durable products by leveraging existing precision manufacturing platform.**
- **Use net proceeds of the Fresh Issue to repay/prepay outstanding borrowings of the Company and three wholly-owned subsidiaries.**
- **Fund capital expenditure on purchase of machinery and equipment by the Company and subsidiary AeroStructures Manufacturing India Private Limited.**
- **Establish and expand electronics manufacturing services line for precision sensor modules and control units under the Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors and State incentives.**
- **Increase procurement of raw materials from domestic suppliers to reduce raw material costs and improve margins.**

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [JV / new vertical] Entered a JV with Accel India Fund and Vagus to set up Ajna Aerospace, focused on UAV manufacturing — a new end-market adjacent to the existing aerostructures base.
- [Reporting basis] The company reports a parallel 'including JV share' view (100% of Aequs plus 50% of API, SQuAD and ACPL and 33% of Ajna), so headline consolidated figures understate platform-level scale.
- [Listing] Entered public markets with a listing in 2025; NSE symbol AEQUS, BSE code 544634.
- [Leadership] Founder-led — Executive Chairman/CEO Aravind Melligeri and Co-founder/MD Rajeev Kaul have both been with the company since its incorporation in 2000.
